findings.evidence: The first-release branch specifies `git log --first-parent --format='%h%x09%s' <to>`, omitting the bodies required by the merge-title extraction on line 35. The breaking-change scan on line 42 still uses `<from>..<to>`, although this branch has no start ref.
findings.fix: Define first-release mode consistently: retain `%h%x09%s%x09%b` when collecting commits, run both collection and breaking-change scanning against `<to>` without a range, and provide first-release wording for the all-filtered stop message.

findings.evidence: "If the tag resolves to the same commit as `HEAD`, rerun from `HEAD^` and use the older tag as the start." This retry does not explicitly reapply stable-tag validation, and `HEAD^` does not exist when the tagged HEAD is a root commit; that error is not covered by the listed describe-failure branches.
findings.fix: Route every retry through the same stable-tag validation loop. Before following a parent, check that it exists; if history is exhausted, use the shallow-check/first-release fallback rather than leaving the branch unresolved.

findings.evidence: "A subject without a conventional prefix goes under Internal." Prefixed commits such as `build: update packaging` or `style: normalize formatting` match none of the listed groups and do not satisfy this fallback.
findings.fix: Make Internal the explicit catch-all for every retained commit not already classified as breaking, feature or fix, including build, style and custom conventional-commit types.

findings.evidence: "`--first-parent` yields one line per merged PR in both merge-commit and squash workflows; `--no-merges` lists every feature-branch commit." This repeats familiar flag explanations alongside the collection command and the more useful, specific warning on line 91.
findings.fix: Delete this explanatory sentence; retain the exact collection command and the specific NEVER warning about combining `--no-merges` with `--first-parent`.
